h1: Khwanruen Fishing Resort — A Fishing Resort Near U-Tapao That Sells Quiet and Gentle Prices
intro: Picture this: dropping a fishing line at the pond on a still-cool morning, hearing more birdsong than traffic, then walking back into a cold air-conditioned room at a small resort just over ten minutes' drive from U-Tapao Airport — Khwanruen Fishing Resort is a 3-star stay beside a fishing pond in Samnak Thon, Ban Chang District, within the southern Pattaya–U-Tapao tourism zone · what many people talk about is the peace and quiet, spacious rooms, cold AC and affordable prices, starting at around THB 700/night · there's a pool, a waterside restaurant, a barbecue area and free parking · the average review score sits around 8.1 from about 136 reviews.

body.html: Who Khwanruen Fishing Resort is right for — to put it as briefly as possible, Khwanruen Fishing Resort is a stay for people who want "peace and quiet at a gentle price" more than luxury or the kind of facilities you'd find at a city hotel · it isn't a beachfront resort where you open the door onto the sand, and it isn't a high-rise hotel with a smart lobby in downtown Pattaya · it's a small 3-star resort sitting beside a fishing pond in Samnak Thon, Ban Chang District — the border zone between Chonburi's southern Pattaya side and Rayong — close to U-Tapao International Airport · real reviews agree that the people who fit here fall into just a few clear groups · the first is travellers flying in and out of U-Tapao who want a quiet bed near the airport for the night before an early flight or the night they land late · the second is fishing lovers who want to wake up and drop a line straight away without driving anywhere · and the third is families or couples looking for a quiet, budget-friendly base before heading to Pattaya, Ramayana Water Park or Mae Ramphueng Beach · those after nightlife, a sea view from the room, or five-star service may find it off the mark and should look at a downtown Pattaya hotel instead · the main selling point is atmosphere and value, not luxury — something worth setting your expectations on before you book.

Location and getting there — Khwanruen's location needs a little explaining, because many platforms file this resort under Pattaya/Chonburi stays, but administratively the resort actually sits in Samnak Thon, Ban Chang District, Rayong Province, the border zone between southern Chonburi and Rayong · the clearest advantage is that it's only about 8–10 kilometres from U-Tapao International Airport (UTP), or roughly a 10–15 minute drive · if you fly low-cost in and out of U-Tapao and don't want a long ride into downtown Pattaya, this location handles staying near the airport well · there are also a few points of interest within a short drive, such as the Eastern Star golf course and the Navy's Plutaluang golf course within a few kilometres, Ramayana Water Park about 6–7 kilometres away, and the town of Ban Chang with its convenience stores, market and restaurants about 6–7 kilometres out · Mae Ramphueng Beach and the boat pier to Koh Samet are also within a not-too-distant drive · one important note: the place is fairly quiet and set back from the main road, and several reviews say the entrance signage isn't clear, so finding your way in the first time can be a little confusing · and since it isn't on the beach or in the town centre, getting around without your own car is hard, so rent one or arrange a ride in advance, as Grab in this zone may not be as plentiful as in downtown Pattaya.

"Landed at U-Tapao in the evening, drove just over ten minutes and we were there. Nice and quiet, slept well, woke up and walked around the fishing pond. Great for the night before or after a flight. The only thing was finding the entrance the first time — the signs aren't very clear, so check the map carefully."

Room types and decor — Khwanruen Fishing Resort is a small resort with roughly 40–54 rooms (the figure varies slightly by platform), laid out as single- and two-storey buildings spread across grounds beside the pond and garden · most rooms are standard, about 26 square metres, with a choice of twin, double, and rooms for three, suiting small families or groups of friends · the decor is a simple upcountry resort style, nothing flashy, focused on being practical and clean · every room has air conditioning, a fridge, a TV, a balcony or private sitting area, and an en-suite bathroom with a water heater · the point real reviews praise most is that the rooms are more spacious than expected for the price, the AC is icy cold, and cleanliness is good · many also mention the good water pressure in the bathroom, so showers run smoothly without trouble — a detail many budget resorts don't get right · that said, to be straight about it, some reviews note that certain rooms are starting to show their age, with wear on some woodwork or furniture, and the AC in some rooms is noisy or doesn't cool as evenly from room to room · the tip is that if room condition matters to you, ask the resort for a recently renovated room or one near the pond/garden for the best view and atmosphere.

Facilities and the pool — even as a small, budget resort, Khwanruen has the basic facilities covered for an easygoing stay · the highlight, true to the resort's name, is the on-site fishing pond where guests can drop a line — an activity that suits anglers or families who want the kids to try something outdoors · there's also an outdoor pool (open during the daytime, roughly 8 AM to evening) to cool off in, a barbecue area that groups of friends or families can book to grill, and a karaoke room for those who like to socialise · there are garden lawns and a waterside terrace to sit out and catch the breeze, plus a kids' area in part of the grounds · other basic services include a reception desk with long opening hours, free parking on spacious grounds, free Wi-Fi, laundry service, and an airport transfer (for a fee) · to be honest, the pool and facilities here are upcountry-resort style, not an infinity pool or an air-conditioned gym like a city hotel — they're more of a space to relax and do outdoor activities than anything luxurious, but in terms of value and atmosphere they do well for this price.

Food and the restaurant — the resort has an on-site waterside restaurant serving Thai food and à la carte dishes, with seating looking out over the pond and garden — a spot many people like because you can eat a relaxed dinner by the water without driving anywhere · for breakfast, it's mostly a package included with the room or paid for separately, simple dishes like rice soup, congee, eggs and bread — reviews call it a homey breakfast that fills you up enough to start the day · one thing to know: if you have to set off early for a flight at U-Tapao, you can ask the resort about a packed breakfast or shifting the timing · a point that comes up in some reviews is that certain dishes come out strongly seasoned/salty for some people, which is a matter of cooking and personal taste, so it's worth saying how salty or spicy you want it when you order · since the resort is fairly far from restaurants outside the grounds, having a kitchen on site is a plus for dinner, but if you want more variety you can drive into the town of Ban Chang in a short time.

Service — service is a point that earns consistent praise in real reviews · the phrase that shows up most often is "friendly staff", looking after guests warmly like a family resort rather than the stiff formality of a big hotel · many praise the help with directions, the airport transfer arrangements, and the flexibility on check-in and check-out times when given notice — which matters a lot for people on a late-arriving or early-departing flight · because it's a small resort, communicating with the owner or staff is direct and quick · the trade-off is that, with a small team, service can slow down a bit when several groups of guests are in at once, and some extra services may not be as complete as at a city hotel · overall, service here is a strength that leaves many guests feeling they got more than they paid for.

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulling from Booking.com, Traveloka and reviews on Thai travel sites, the picture is fairly consistent, with an average score around 8.1 from about 136 reviews · On the praise side: very affordable and great value, rooms more spacious than expected, cold AC, clean rooms, good water pressure, a quiet atmosphere that's great for relaxing, friendly staff, and a handy location near U-Tapao Airport for people flying in and out · the fishing activity and waterside atmosphere are also a point many families say the kids enjoy · On the cautionary side: the most frequently mentioned issue is the unclear entrance signage, which makes finding the way in the first time hard · next is the AC in some rooms cooling unevenly or being noisy, certain rooms starting to show their age, and some dishes being too strongly seasoned/salty for some people · on top of that, people without their own car often complain about the inconvenient travel in and out, as there's no public transport right at the spot · most of these gripes are things you can manage with advance planning and the right expectations, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back.

"For this price it's great value — spacious room, cold AC, clean, lovely staff. The fishing pond kept the kids happily trying to catch something. The only downsides are that it'd be hard without your own car, and the entrance is a bit tricky to find. Next time I'll have the coordinates ready."

Price and value — the starting price for a standard room is around THB 700/night in normal periods (some promotions go a little lower), rising to about THB 900–1,300 over long weekends or festivals · rooms for three or higher-capacity rooms sit in the low thousands depending on size and timing · compared with other stays near U-Tapao Airport or in the Ban Chang zone, Khwanruen feels very good value among budget stays, especially when you factor in the spacious rooms, the quiet atmosphere, the on-site pool and fishing pond, and a location that saves time getting to the airport · if your goal is "a clean, quiet bed near U-Tapao for a few hundred baht" or "a quiet base before heading to Pattaya–Rayong," every baht you spend comes back in full · but if you compare it with a downtown Pattaya hotel that has the sea, nightlife and restaurants within walking distance, you have to accept this is a different kind of stay — choose based mainly on your trip style.

Things to know before you book — there are several things that make the stay smoother · One, have your GPS coordinates ready and study the map carefully before setting off, because the entrance signage is unclear and finding the way in the first time can be confusing, especially if you arrive at night · Two, this place suits people with their own car best — if you don't have one, plan for the airport transfer or arrange a ride in advance, as there's no public transport right at the spot and Grab can be hard to find · Three, make the most of the location near U-Tapao — if your flight lands late or leaves early, this is a base that saves time and money compared with staying in downtown Pattaya · Four, if room condition matters to you, ask for a recently renovated room or one beside the pond/garden for the best atmosphere · Five, when ordering food you can say how salty or spicy you'd like it so it suits your taste, and if you have to leave early, give advance notice about breakfast · Six, book ahead over long weekends, because it's a small resort with a limited number of rooms.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Khwanruen Fishing Resort is the stay best suited to people looking for a clean, quiet, affordable bed near U-Tapao Airport and those who want the simple atmosphere of a resort beside a fishing pond · spacious rooms, cold AC, friendly staff, an on-site pool and fishing pond, and an affordable price make it good value among the budget stays of the Ban Chang zone · if you fly in and out of U-Tapao often, or want a quiet base before heading to Pattaya–Rayong, this place meets that need well at a price that's hard to match · but if you're after a sea view from the room, nightlife, five-star service, or getting around without your own car, this may not be the answer, and a downtown Pattaya hotel is worth considering instead · in short, Khwanruen is a small resort that knows its own place well — selling quiet, value and proximity to the airport in a way that's straightforward and honest.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Khwanruen Fishing Resort

faq.q: Where is Khwanruen Fishing Resort · is it near U-Tapao Airport?
faq.a: The resort is in Samnak Thon, Ban Chang District, Rayong Province, within the southern Pattaya–U-Tapao border tourism zone · it's only about 8–10 kilometres from U-Tapao International Airport (UTP), a 10–15 minute drive · close to the Plutaluang and Eastern Star golf courses and Ramayana Water Park within a short drive · note that the entrance signage is unclear, so have your GPS coordinates ready.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Khwanruen Fishing Resort · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 700/night for a standard room of about 26 sqm in normal periods · there are double-bed rooms, twin rooms, and rooms for three, good for a small family · prices over long weekends or festivals rise to about THB 900–1,300, so book ahead as it's a small resort with limited rooms.

faq.q: Who is Khwanruen Fishing Resort right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers flying in and out of U-Tapao, fishing lovers, and families/couples wanting a quiet, affordable stay as a base before exploring Pattaya–Rayong · it has a fishing pond, a pool and an on-site restaurant · if you're after a sea view from the room, nightlife, or five-star service, a downtown Pattaya hotel may suit you better.

faq.q: Without my own car, is it convenient to stay at Khwanruen?
faq.a: Straight up, this place suits people with their own car best, because it's set back from the main road, there's no public transport right at the spot, and Grab in this zone can be hard to find · if you don't have a car, we recommend booking the resort's airport transfer (for a fee) or renting a car in advance.

faq.q: Does Khwanruen Fishing Resort really have a pool and a fishing pond?
faq.a: It has both · an on-site fishing pond where guests can drop a line, true to the resort's name, and an outdoor pool open during the daytime · there's also a barbecue area, a karaoke room, a waterside restaurant, free parking and free Wi-Fi · these are upcountry-resort facilities focused on comfort and outdoor activities.

faq.q: What are the food and service like at Khwanruen?
faq.a: The resort has a waterside restaurant serving à la carte Thai food, and breakfast that's either included or paid for separately (rice soup, congee, eggs, bread) · real reviews praise the friendly staff, well looked after like a family resort · a point that comes up is that some dishes are strongly seasoned/salty, so it's worth saying how you'd like it when you order, and if you leave early, give advance notice about breakfast.
